title: Global monetary divergence persists while RBI locks money-market rates and presses regulatory resets
changed: Monetary divergence deepened across major central banks this week. In the United States, Q2 GDP slowing to 2.2% lifted expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts and offered temporary relief to emerging market currencies, even as climbing US 10-year yields sparked mid-week equity declines. Concurrently, European Central Bank leadership reiterated a higher-for-longer path amid persistent inflation shocks, while the Bank of Japan advanced policy normalisation after a strong Tankan print pointed to sustained corporate strength, raising risks of yen carry trade unwinds.

Energy pressures evolved as early-week risks around a blocked Hormuz diplomatic channel kept a geopolitical risk premium in Brent crude. That upward pressure was partially blunted later in the week by record US natural gas production and a coordinated G7 fuel release that offset threats of US diesel export restrictions, limiting wholesale fuel volatility for energy importers.

Domestically, the Reserve Bank of India maintained a restrictive liquidity stance, conducting successive ₹2 lakh crore Variable Rate Reverse Repo auctions and fixing the floor near 5.24%. Alongside the fiscal deficit reaching ₹7.10 lakh crore (42% of the FY27 target), the RBI absorbed liquidity to maintain upward pressure on short-term rates. Concurrently, it initiated a Benchmark Issuance Strategy pilot for State Development Loans to compress sub-sovereign spreads after state auctions cleared between 7.4% and 8.0%.

For banks and non-bank lenders, systemic pressures intensified around the credit-deposit divergence highlighted in the RBI Bulletin. The central bank raised capital charges by tightening classification and valuation norms on financial institution investment portfolios, raising balance sheet provisioning hurdles as retail deposit competition mounts.

On compliance and corporate finance operations, the regulatory landscape shifted across multiple fronts. SEBI settled its long-running probe into Adani Group alongside actions on alternative investment fund structures and listed disclosure mandates. Meanwhile, the RBI eliminated transactional size caps on online Form A2 outward remittances, shifted NRI deposit reporting to the CIMS Sankalan portal, and tightened acquisition and voting rules for Local Area Banks.

threads.name: RBI liquidity absorption and bank funding
threads.note: Back-to-back ₹2 lakh crore VRRR auctions anchor money market floors near 5.24% while credit-deposit gaps compress bank margins. Continued net liquidity drains or further tightening of FI portfolio capital rules will confirm sustained margin strain.

threads.name: Global central bank divergence
threads.note: US deceleration to 2.2% supports Fed easing prospects, contrasting with ECB higher-for-longer messaging and BoJ normalization. Discrepancies between US growth prints and resilient European inflation indicators will dictate the trajectory of USD and emerging market capital flows.

threads.name: Indian sovereign and sub-sovereign yield curves
threads.note: State bond auctions yielding up to 8% and a fiscal deficit at 42% of the FY27 target weigh on G-sec paper. The success of the RBI's Benchmark Issuance Strategy pilot will determine if state development loan spreads compress against the 10-year benchmark.

threads.name: Cross-border compliance and exchange controls
threads.note: FEMA export-import documentation updates and relaxed online Form A2 thresholds alter trade and capital-account administrative timelines. Further operational transitions onto the CIMS portal will determine execution drag for corporate and retail flows.
